title: Growing Einstein-Rosen Bridge with Multi-partite Entanglement
authors: Takanori Anegawa, Akihiro Miyata, Shota Suzuki, Kotaro Tamaoka
abstract: Can quantum entanglement continue to grow even after the entanglement entropies of subsystems have saturated? We address this question using genuine multi-entropy, which probes multi-partite entanglement structure beyond bipartite entanglement. In a two-sided BTZ black hole, this quantity grows linearly with time after every subsystem entropy of a fixed tripartition has saturated, extending the interval in which entanglement detects Einstein-Rosen bridge growth. The result refines the ER=EPR relation by identifying multi-partite structure invisible to ordinary entanglement entropies. Some spin-chain models and the spatially partitioned Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model exhibit distinct transients, while the late-time plateau values in holography, the SYK model, and Haar-random states share a universal behaviour.
summary: This work explores the role of multi-partite entanglement in detecting the growth of an Einstein-Rosen bridge, refining the ER=EPR conjecture. By using genuine multi-entropy, the authors show that entanglement can continue to grow in black hole analogues even when standard entanglement entropies saturate. This suggests that multi-partite structure is necessary to fully characterize the quantum correlations underlying spacetime connectivity.
main_problem: The research investigates whether quantum entanglement can continue to grow in a system, specifically an Einstein-Rosen bridge, even after the standard entanglement entropies of its subsystems have saturated.
main_result: Genuine multi-entropy can grow linearly with time in the holographic description of a two-sided BTZ black hole, extending the regime where entanglement detects ER bridge growth beyond what bipartite entanglement measures can capture.
method: The authors employ genuine multi-entropy ($	ext{GM}(3)$) and compare its time evolution against standard entanglement entropy calculations derived from the Ryu-Takayanagi (HRT) prescription in AdS/CFT.
model_or_system: The primary systems studied include the two-sided BTZ black hole (dual to a TFD state), the spatially partitioned Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model, and general spin-chain models.
key_observables: Genuine multi-entropy ($	ext{GM}(3)$), entanglement entropy ($S$), and mutual information ($I$).
important_parameters: Time ($t$), black hole parameters ($r_+, L$), and the number of subsystems (tripartition).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the high-temperature limit ($ eta 	o 0$) for the holographic calculations and compares results across different Rényi indices ($n$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dynamical phases of multi-entropy growth in the holographic setup, comparing the multi-entropy network evolution against the HRT surface evolution, and showing time evolution comparisons between $	ext{GM}(3)$ and mutual information in various models.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the problem using multi-partite entanglement measures, applying these measures to holographic models (BTZ black hole) to refine the ER=EPR relation, and then validating these findings by comparing the dynamics across different quantum many-body systems like SYK and spin chains.
why_interesting: The focus on multi-partite entanglement provides a powerful diagnostic tool to probe non-local quantum correlations that are essential for understanding spacetime geometry (ER bridges) in quantum gravity contexts.
